evals.prompt: Use opencode to build the CSV export feature in docs/plans/csv-export.md for the jobs app. You orchestrate.
evals.expected_output: Reads the plan and CLAUDE.md, creates .orchestra/<run>/ with config defaults, writes an efficient task table in board.md (few small tasks, disjoint files for parallel runs, dependencies only where needed, exact test commands) and starts dispatching without asking the user to approve the table.
assertions: Creates .orchestra/<run>/ and board.md with a task table
Each task lists files, dependencies and an exact test command
Concurrent tasks have disjoint files
Starts dispatching without asking the user to approve the task table

evals.prompt: Here's the approved task table: T1 adds export_csv() in api/export.py, T2 adds the /export route in api/routes.py, T3 adds a button in web/src/Jobs.tsx and also edits api/routes.py. Concurrency is 2. Start dispatching.
evals.expected_output: Notices T2 and T3 both change api/routes.py and serializes them (dependency) instead of running them together; dispatches at most 2 non-overlapping ready tasks; respects T2 depending on T1 if stated.
assertions: Identifies that T2 and T3 both change api/routes.py
Prevents T2 and T3 from changing api/routes.py at the same time (adds a dependency, or moves the routes.py edit into one task)
Never has more than 2 tasks dispatched at once
Keeps T2 after T1 when that dependency is stated

evals.prompt: T4 came back rejected for the third time (max_rejections is 3). What now?
evals.expected_output: Takes the task over instead of a fourth dispatch: picks the cheapest capable Claude model (haiku/sonnet/opus per the model ladder) as a subagent in the same worktree, reviews its result with tests, marks it taken-over with the model in board.md.
assertions: Does not dispatch T4 a fourth time
Takes the task over with the cheapest capable model (haiku or sonnet, not opus by default)
The takeover result is reviewed with tests before merging
Marks T4 taken-over with the model in board.md

evals.prompt: The session crashed halfway through the orchestration run. Pick it up again.
evals.expected_output: Reads .orchestra/<run>/board.md, checks dispatched tasks' worktrees for RESULT.md or a live run, and continues the loop from the recorded state rather than starting over.
assertions: Reads .orchestra/<run>/board.md first
Checks dispatched tasks for a live run or RESULT.md in their worktree
Continues from the recorded state instead of starting a new run

evals.prompt: T2 was rejected once and T5 twice. Should either be taken over?
evals.expected_output: No: both go back to opencode with review notes (--continue); takeover only after the third rejection.
assertions: Takes over neither T2 nor T5
Sends both back to opencode with review notes (--continue)
States takeover happens only after the 3rd rejection

evals.prompt: Find the todo task 'Research app (headless runner + web UI)' and use claude-orchestrate-development to build it. The repo is empty apart from the devcontainer.
evals.expected_output: Notices there is no written plan (no docs/plans/, only a todo task) and does not create .orchestra/ or a task graph yet: runs brainstorming with the user to settle the design (stack, scope, hosting), then writing-plans to save a plan in docs/plans/, and only then starts the orchestration run from that plan.
assertions: Does not create .orchestra/ or a task graph
Runs or proposes brainstorming with the user first
Plans writing-plans to save a plan in docs/plans/ before orchestrating
Does not choose the stack/architecture itself

evals.prompt: Plan docs/plans/2026-11-23-export-plan.md has phases 1-3. Orchestrate it. (T1 and T2 of phase 1 just came back from opencode.)
evals.expected_output: Keeps source, diffs, test output and logs out of its own thread: specs and reviews go to subagents (spec_model / review_model, opus for tasks marked review: opus) that reply with one line; reviews run one at a time; small bugs go back as notes rather than being fixed inline. When phase 1 is all merged it runs an opus code-review over the phase diff, logs it, and stops, telling the user to start a new session with 'resume run <run>'.
assertions: Does not read diffs, source files, test output or logs in the orchestrator thread
Delegates specs and reviews to subagents with a named model (spec_model/review_model or sonnet)
Expects or requests one-line replies from the subagents
Sends small bugs back as review notes instead of fixing them inline
At the end of phase 1 runs a phase-level review on opus over the phase diff
Stops after phase 1 and tells the user to start a new session to resume the run

evals.prompt: The plan has a task 'add the constant MAX_ROWS = 500 to config.py'. Dispatch it to opencode.
evals.expected_output: Doesn't dispatch a task whose spec would be as long as its code: merges it into the neighbouring task that uses MAX_ROWS (or has it done there), and keeps the task graph small.
assertions: Does not dispatch the MAX_ROWS constant as its own opencode task
Merges it into the task that uses MAX_ROWS (or does it as part of that task)
Gives the size reason: the spec would be as long as the code
